claim: The OSS OneDrive client for Linux syncs Personal/Business/SharePoint libraries but explicitly does not implement Windows files-on-demand and is CLI-only.
quote: Support for Windows 'On-Demand' functionality so file is only downloaded when accessed locally — listed under 'What's missing'. Supports OneDrive Personal, OneDrive for Business and Microsoft SharePoint Libraries; all major Linux distributions, FreeBSD and OpenBSD.

claim: First-hand March 2026 account: Teams wrapper worked identically to Windows, DavMail/OWL solved mail+calendar, but the organisation blocked both popular open-source OneDrive clients from signing in and no client offers files-on-demand.
quote: OneDrive Sync: This remained the major pain point. Native Linux clients lack files-on-demand functionality, while the author's organization blocked both popular open-source solutions from signing in. functionality is _exactly_ the same as on windows

claim: Obsidian's official OneNote importer supports only personal Microsoft accounts; work/school notebooks and locked sections cannot be imported.
quote: Only notebooks owned by your personal account can be imported. Work and school accounts are not supported. Locked sections remain invisible during import unless unlocked first.

claim: Microsoft's own Teams client availability matrix (updated 16 Jul 2026) marks Linux as not supported and lists Web as the supported route.
quote: | Linux | ❌ | Teams is no longer supported on Linux. | | Web | ✅ | Supported in Microsoft Edge, Chrome, Firefox, Safari. |

claim: Evolution maintainer confirms (3 Jul 2026) that Microsoft 365 Graph API accounts are available in Evolution 3.60.x via evolution-ews, past preview stage, but without full EWS feature parity.
quote: You install evolution-ews, which adds you both 'Exchange Web Services' and 'Microsoft 365' account options. The 'preview mode' was in time of 3.52/3.56.x series...Since then many main pain points had been fixed. The protocols are different and the feature parity is not complete.

claim: Power Query in Excel for the web: viewing/refreshing for all Microsoft 365 subscribers, full authoring for Business/Enterprise plans, with a listed set of supported sources.
quote: Viewing and refreshing are available to all Microsoft 365 subscribers. Additional functionality is available to all Microsoft 365 Subscribers with Business or Enterprise plans.

claim: The full Power Query experience (import wizard plus editor) reached Excel for the web in January 2026; desktop still wins on local file sources, the full connector library and heavy M work.
quote: The desktop still wins at the edges: local file sources, the full connector library, complex pipelines with heavy data volumes, and anything requiring advanced M language work beyond the standard interface.

claim: 2026 survey of Office-on-Linux options: no native Office exists; browser Office is officially supported but VBA does not run; open-source suites break on complex layouts and macro-heavy files; a Windows VM is the power-user option.
quote: VBA macros don't run. Many advanced Excel features are missing or simplified. ... once you start dealing with complex Word layouts, large Excel models or macro-heavy files, compatibility gaps become obvious.

claim: ONLYOFFICE macros are JavaScript against the Document Builder API, not VBA.
quote: ONLYOFFICE macros use JavaScript language syntax and ONLYOFFICE Document Builder API scripting notation.

claim: Thunderbird 145 shipped native Exchange (EWS) email support, removing the need for third-party add-ons for mail; calendar and address book remain on the roadmap.
quote: Thunderbird users in Microsoft Exchange environments no longer need third-party add-ons... Calendar and address book support for Exchange accounts remain on the roadmap, but email integration is here and ready to use.

claim: EWS is disabled by default in Exchange Online on 1 Oct 2026 and fully shut down 1 Apr 2027; admin allow-lists must be configured before end of August 2026.
quote: The API will be disabled by default on October 1, 2026, and will be completely shut down on April 1, 2027, with 'no exceptions.' ... they must do so by the end of August 2026, or they'll lose access to EWS on the cutoff date.

claim: Microsoft announced GA of the Teams PWA for Linux as a feature of the web client.
quote: Microsoft has announced general availability of support for the Microsoft Teams progressive web app (PWA) as a feature of the current web client for Linux customers.

claim: DavMail 6.8 exposes Microsoft Graph mode in the GUI with mandatory OAuth2 (MFA/Conditional Access compatible) and can auto-create Teams meetings via the CalDAV online-meeting setting.
quote: DavMail 6.8 brings active Microsoft Graph support into the GUI... mandatory OAuth 2.0 authentication ensures compatibility with MFA and Conditional Access policies. Automatic Teams meeting creation through the CalDAV online-meeting setting closes a practical gap.

claim: Thunderbird cannot natively create invitations recognised as Microsoft Teams meetings; it is an open feature request.
quote: Currently there's no way for meetings sent from Thunderbird to be recognized as MS Teams meetings.

claim: The Microsoft 365 (Office) app became the Microsoft 365 Copilot app, reachable in any browser at m365.cloud.microsoft, with office.com and microsoft365.com redirecting.
quote: The Microsoft 365 (Office) app is now called the Microsoft 365 Copilot app. The web URL has been updated to m365.cloud.microsoft... Both office.com and microsoft365.com URLs will automatically redirect.

claim: There is no first-party OneDrive client for Linux; abraunegg is the gold-standard OSS daemon, onedriver has limited SharePoint support, and Insync is claimed to have dropped OneDrive in 2024.
quote: There is no first-party OneDrive for Linux client. Microsoft hasn't shipped one in 15 years and probably won't... Insync used to, dropped support in 2024.

claim: Dropbox's current Linux requirements: Ubuntu 18.04+/Fedora 28+, ext4, zfs, eCryptFS backed by ext4, xfs and btrfs, 64-bit only, no ARM.
quote: Supported filesystems: ext4, zfs, eCryptFS (backed by ext4), xfs, btrfs. Dropbox doesn't support ARM processors for Linux.

claim: In 2018 Dropbox announced it would sync only on ext4 on Linux from 7 November 2018.
quote: Dropbox announced that starting on November 7th 2018, only the ext4 file system would be supported in Linux for synchronizing folders in the Dropbox desktop app.

claim: Dropbox partially reversed the ext4-only restriction in July 2019, re-adding zfs, eCryptFS, xfs and btrfs.
quote: Add support for zfs (on 64-bit systems only), eCryptFS, xfs (on 64-bit systems only), and btrfs filesystems in Linux.

claim: LibreOffice 26.2 was released 4 February 2026 with a focus on performance, interoperability and file formats.
quote: LibreOffice 26.2 is here: a faster, more polished office suite that you control — the Document Foundation's first major release of 2026 focuses on performance, interoperability and file formats.

claim: Obsidian ships official Linux builds as AppImage, Snap, deb, Flatpak and an ARM64 AppImage.
quote: Obsidian offers multiple Linux installation formats: AppImage, Snap, Deb, AppImage (AArch64/ARM64), and Flatpak.

claim: Anthropic released Claude Desktop for Linux in beta on 30 June 2026 for Ubuntu 22.04+/Debian 12+ with an apt repo; Computer Use and voice dictation are missing.
quote: Anthropic released the beta of its Claude desktop app for Linux alongside an apt repo Ubuntu users can add for ongoing updates. The Linux beta lacks Computer Use... and voice dictation.

claim: The Copilot Desktop snap for Linux is an unofficial community web wrapper published by Ken VanDine, last updated 9 February 2026.
quote: Unofficial Web app for Microsoft Copilot providing the desktop user experience you would expect on Ubuntu or any other Linux desktop. Publisher: Ken VanDine. Last updated: February 9, 2026.

claim: Wayland screen sharing needs three layers (xdg-desktop-portal backend, PipeWire, app pointed at portal capture); the Teams PWA in Chrome/Edge handles capture better than the Electron client.
quote: The fix for Wayland screen sharing has three layers: installing the right XDG Desktop Portal backend for your compositor, checking that PipeWire is running as your media daemon, and setting your browser or app to use the portal capture path.

claim: On Ubuntu 26 with GNOME/Wayland, screen sharing fails in the teams-for-linux snap build ('Bind context provider failed') while the .deb works, indicating snap confinement blocks the xdg-desktop-portal ScreenCast call.
quote: Screen sharing fails in snap build on Wayland — 'Bind context provider failed'. ... suggests snap confinement is blocking the xdg-desktop-portal ScreenCast call rather than a code issue, as the .deb package works fine.

claim: Uploading custom meeting backgrounds is limited in the Teams web/PWA client on Linux, though blur and predefined backgrounds work.
quote: While there are options for blurring and choosing a pre-defined set of backgrounds, custom background uploads are limited on Linux PWA.

claim: Fedora users report Teams PWA background filters not working at all.
quote: Microsoft Teams PWA - Background filters does not work

claim: Long-running Microsoft Q&A thread documenting Teams PWA notification problems on Linux: silent notifications, toasts self-deleting after ~5 seconds, missing meeting-started alerts.
quote: Notifications show up briefly but automatically delete themselves after about 5 seconds. Some notification types, like 'meeting started' notifications, don't display, causing users to miss meetings.

claim: teams-for-linux is an unofficial Electron wrapper of the Teams web app adding system notifications, tray, custom backgrounds, screen sharing and multi-account profiles, with contextIsolation and sandbox disabled.
quote: This is an independent project, not affiliated with Microsoft. Some features are limited by the Teams web app. ... developers disable Electron's contextIsolation and sandbox features to enable Teams DOM access functionality.

claim: Microsoft's official announcement of EWS retirement in Exchange Online, directing developers to Microsoft Graph.
quote: Retirement of Exchange Web Services in Exchange Online — Microsoft is retiring the longstanding Exchange Web Services (EWS) in Exchange Online, directing developers to Microsoft Graph.

claim: June 2026: Thunderbird's Graph implementation is entering the final stretch toward EWS parity, calendar integration is only being planned, and Microsoft confirmed approved mail clients can obtain previously unavailable consent.
quote: now entering the final stretch toward feature parity with our existing EWS implementation ... Microsoft confirmed that approved mail clients such as Thunderbird will continue to be able to obtain user consent for permissions that were previously unavailable to third-party applications.

claim: Thunderbird's desktop roadmap lists Exchange (EWS, GraphAPI) including calendar and address book as active work, with Exchange email support shipped November 2025.
quote: Exchange (EWS, GraphAPI) Finalize the work on the Exchange protocol in order to support all versions of Exchange and Microsoft 365, including calendar and address book support. ... Exchange Email Support ... November 2025

claim: Owl for Exchange is a paid Thunderbird add-on at 10 EUR/year that syncs calendar and address books and supports MFA.
quote: OWL is a paid extension with a price of 10€/year. The OWL extension allows synchronization of Calendar and address books ... and has support for multi-factor authentication (MFA).

claim: Betterbird's stable line in July 2026 is 140.13.0esr-bb25 (pre-EWS), while the newer 153.0esr-bb6 build carries a do-not-use-in-production warning.
quote: 140.13.0esr-bb25 (July 21, 2026) ... 153.0esr-bb6 (July 20, 2026) — we're just starting to gain experience with the new 153 series, so please do not use this version in production yet.

claim: Local (non-cloud) notebooks are a OneNote desktop-only feature; the web app is cloud-only.
quote: The desktop app is the only OneNote version that supports local notebook storage on your PC in addition to cloud storage.

claim: P3X OneNote is an actively released Electron wrapper of OneNote for Linux; 2026 releases added an 'Auto (system)' language option for locale detection.
quote: Linux Electron Onenote - A Linux compatible version of OneNote. Version v2026.4.127 released on 04/04/2026 added 'Auto (system)' language option for automatic locale detection.

claim: onenote-md-exporter is a Windows console app that exports OneNote notebooks to Markdown (via Word DOCX + Pandoc) with Joplin and Obsidian output targets.
quote: ConsoleApp to export OneNote notebooks to Markdown formats ... It first exports each page as a DOCX file using Word, then converts those files to Markdown using Pandoc, resulting in a clean folder structure where sections become folders and pages become .md files.

claim: Known losses when exporting OneNote to Markdown in 2026: handwriting, text tags, password-protected sections and images nested in tables.
quote: Handwriting and text tags don't survive the conversion, password-protected sections get skipped unless you unlock them first, and if you have images nested inside tables, they might not export correctly.

claim: Without --vfs-cache-mode writes or full, an rclone mount cannot do random writes or seek-on-read, so many applications will not work with files on the mount.
quote: rclone can only write files sequentially and seek when reading, meaning many applications won't work with their files on an rclone mount without --vfs-cache-mode writes or --vfs-cache-mode full.

claim: onedriver is a native FUSE filesystem for OneDrive giving on-demand file access; last pushed January 2026.
quote: A native Linux filesystem for Microsoft OneDrive. pushed_at 2026-01-31

claim: Insync's own Linux page currently advertises OneDrive support including SharePoint, OneDrive for Business and Dropbox Team folders.
quote: Insync for Linux supports Google Drive, OneDrive (including SharePoint, OneDrive for Business, and Dropbox Team folders) and Dropbox.

claim: The abraunegg client's Entra app registration shows as unverified and requests broad delegated scopes, which is what tenant admins object to.
quote: a feature request asking about ways to verify the app so it does not say 'unverified' ... concerns about requesting broad access permissions like 'Edit or delete all site collections' and 'Have full access to all files user can access'.

claim: Beyond interactive browser OAuth2, the client supports Intune SSO via the Microsoft Identity Device Broker D-Bus interface and the OAuth2 device authorisation flow for Entra ID.
quote: alternative authentication methods available outside the default interactive browser-based OAuth2 process, including Single Sign-On (SSO) via Intune using the Microsoft Identity Device Broker D-Bus interface and OAuth2 Device Authorisation Flow for Microsoft Entra ID accounts.

claim: Excel for the web does not run macros, does not render ActiveX/form controls, and refuses to display workbooks with workbook-level IRM or digital signatures.
quote: Macros do not run in a browser window ... ActiveX controls and form toolbar controls don't display on the grid ... workbooks with Information Rights Management (IRM) settings applied at the workbook level cannot be viewed in a browser window ... Digital signatures prevent browser viewing.

claim: ONLYOFFICE deliberately does not support VBA macros; its JavaScript macros are sandboxed with no system access.
quote: ONLYOFFICE uses JavaScript for macros for security reasons, as macros do not have any access to the system... ONLYOFFICE doesn't support Visual Basic (VBA) macros, as they use a different scripting language.

claim: LibreOffice 26.2 improves Excel interop: BIFF12 clipboard support removing paste size limits, Excel 2010-365 as the default XLSX export target, DOCX floating-table interop and partial OOXML chart-style round-tripping.
quote: Excel interoperability improves significantly with support for the Excel 2007+ (BIFF12) clipboard format, which removes paste size limits, and Excel 2010–365 is now the default XLSX export target.

claim: LibreOffice's own documentation states VBA support is incomplete and that users may need to rewrite macros in LibreOffice Basic; executable VBA requires enabling a Load/Save option.
quote: Support for VBA is not complete, but it covers a large portion of the common usage patterns. ... you may have to edit the VBA code and complete the missing support with LibreOffice Basic objects, statements and functions. ... enable the 'Executable code' checkbox in Tools - Options - Load/Save - VBA Properties.

claim: LibreOffice UI languages, spell checkers and help are installed as separate per-language packages on Linux and selected under Tools > Options > Language Settings > Languages.
quote: sudo apt install libreoffice-l10n-fr for French on Ubuntu/Debian, or sudo dnf install libreoffice-langpack-fr on Fedora. Language packs ... provide translations for the user interface, spell checker, and help files.
